blocking.section: Runtime / rule 7 and Default limits (Instance pool size, Pool manager, Cold compilation); Performance model / Sizing; Capabilities and sandboxing / audit
blocking.issue: This is a new regression from the round-2 fix. Pool bounds that depend on core count break at both ends of the core range. (1) The parked bound is N minus GOMAXPROCS, with N set by memory and fixed at the default cap, and it has a hard ceiling of 32. At 16 MiB and the default 2 GiB cap, N = floor(512 MiB / 16 MiB) = 32. A 16-core Node therefore gets 16 parked slots, below the 20 that the document's own healthy `state.read` row needs at 20,000 requests per second, and a 16-core Node would normally carry more traffic than that. A Node with 32 or more cores gets 0 parked slots, so every `state_*` call returns ERR_UNAVAILABLE and yields RZ-STS, even at 1 request per second against a healthy State Store. Closed Policies then deny all traffic. The fixed ceiling of 32 also ignores throughput: a large Node at 60,000 requests per second with a 1 ms round trip needs about 60 parked slots. `ruralz bundle audit` runs offline and cannot see GOMAXPROCS, so a Plugin with N >= 32 passes the audit and still fails on large Nodes. (2) At the small end, `GOMAXPROCS`/2 pool-manager workers is 0 when GOMAXPROCS = 1, which is a common Kubernetes CPU limit. With no workers, no instance is ever created and every Plugin call fails with RZ-PLG-005. Likewise, `WithCompilationWorkers` capped at `GOMAXPROCS`/4 gives 0 below 4 cores.
blocking.evidence: Default limits: "at most min(2 × `GOMAXPROCS`, N) computing and, in `state.*` pools, max(0, min(32, N − `GOMAXPROCS`)) parked; warm minimum 1 (target)" and "Share: 25% of the Node cap (target)"; "Node Plugin memory (Gateway `limits.maxPluginMemoryBytes`) | 2 GiB (target)". Rule 7: "beyond the parked bound, or with the State client breaker open, `state_*` returns `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` at once, yielding `RZ-STS`". Sizing: "`state.read` 16 MiB, healthy | 20,000 requests/s, 20 µs plus a 1 ms round trip; N = 32, parked bound 24 on 8 cores | 20 parked (hypothesis)". Audit: "`state.*` Plugins with N below 32 (target)". Pool manager: "`GOMAXPROCS`/2 workers". Cold compilation: "`WithCompilationWorkers` at most `GOMAXPROCS`/4".
blocking.fix: Stop deriving the parked bound from GOMAXPROCS. Reserve a small number of compute slots that does not grow with cores, for example reserved = min(floor(N/4), max(2, ceil(2 × observed compute busy))) (target). Set parked = N − reserved, and either drop the fixed ceiling of 32 or scale it with call rate × `stateStoreTimeout`. The default `maxPluginMemoryBytes` is materialized into the Revision, so it cannot depend on core count. Instead, let the share for `state.*` pools grow (for example, up to 50% of the cap (target)), or state that large Nodes need a larger cap. Because the audit cannot see cores, have the Node emit a degraded metric and log line at activation when a `state.*` pool's parked bound is below a threshold. Use max(1, GOMAXPROCS/2) pool-manager workers and max(1, GOMAXPROCS/4) compile workers. Add Sizing rows for the 16 MiB `state.read` Plugin on 16-core and 32-core Nodes, and correct the audit rule to match.

blocking.section: Runtime / Default limits (Compiled code per Node); Failure semantics and the RZ-PLG registry
blocking.issue: The document calls the Revision-only compiled-code limit a deterministic RZ-CFG-028, but the limit is measured on native compiled code. That size depends on CPU architecture: wazero compiles to amd64 or arm64, and the two produce different code. It also depends on the wazero version, and the research names no API for measuring compiled size. The result therefore does not reproduce from the Revision, which contradicts pack 8.3's definition of a deterministic NACK and pack 8.1's rule that equal digests mean equal behavior. In a Cluster that mixes amd64 and arm64, or where CI links a different wazero, one canary Node can NACK 'deterministically' and trigger `autoRollback` for a Revision that fits on every other Node. The online stage (CI and ingest) also cannot reproduce a number measured on a Node. The round-2 non-blocking note asking how the bound is measured was not addressed, and OQ-wasm-plugin-system-16 does not cover it.
blocking.evidence: Default limits: "Compiled code per Node | 512 MiB (target) | Active and retained snapshots | RZ-CFG-028 when the Revision alone exceeds it; transient NACK while retained code blocks it". Failure semantics: "Deterministic failures reproduce from the Revision and fail the gate at once (pack section 8.3): ... size, structure or Revision-only compiled-code limits". Performance model: "Compiled code per MiB of Wasm | 4 MiB or less (hypothesis)". Pack 8.3: "A deterministic NACK is an `RZ-CFG-<NNN>` error that reproduces from the Revision; it fails the gate at once." Pack 8.1: "Equal digests mean equal effective behavior on every Node that accepts them". Research go-libraries-runtime.md 2.2: "The Compiler (AOT) mode works only on amd64 and arm64" (the research lists no compiled-size API).
blocking.fix: Make the deterministic check a function of the Revision only. For example, RZ-CFG-028 applies when the sum over distinct Plugin digests of artifact bytes × a fixed factor of 4 (matching the hypothesis row) exceeds 512 MiB, or when the Wasm bytes of the Revision alone exceed 128 MiB (target). The online stage and every Node then compute the same answer. Classify an overrun measured on a Node, however it is measured, as a transient NACK plus a degraded metric, never as RZ-CFG-028. State how a Node measures compiled size, for example as the process heap delta around each compile or as a Wasm-size estimate, and add the measurement to OQ-wasm-plugin-system-16.

non_blocking.section: Hot-swap lifecycle / step 4; Performance model / Sizing
non_blocking.suggestion: Pools are keyed per configuration, so one Plugin configured differently on many Routes owns many pools, and upgrading it replaces all of them at once. In the reference Bundle (20 pools, 1.25 GiB), a full replacement needs about 2.5 GiB before the swap, above the 2 GiB cap. About 40% of the new pools would then 'start at 0' and serve RZ-PLG-005 until the replaced pools trim after the swap. For auth and authz Plugins that means 401 or 403 responses. The sentence 'plus swap replacements and headroom' is true only for partial replacements. Qualify that sentence and state the expected rejection window (target). Add a Hot Reload test case that replaces every pool of a many-pool Plugin under load, and an audit finding when one Plugin's aggregate peak exceeds the memory free at swap time.

non_blocking.section: Runtime / Default limits (Fault breaker); Threat model / PT-15
non_blocking.suggestion: The fault breaker is per pool and trips on a ratio, so it amplifies denial of service. On a low-traffic pool, about 101 crafted faulting requests in 10 s trip it, and then 95% of legitimate traffic is denied (closed) or bypassed (open) for 5 s, again and again. PT-15 accepts this, but consider tracking faults per client identity (source address or Consumer) and requiring a minimum number of distinct faulting clients before tripping. Alternatively, for closed auth and authz Plugins, keep calling the guest and rely only on the bounded refill rate.

non_blocking.section: Plugin ABI v1 / WASI shim table
non_blocking.suggestion: `sched_yield` still has no row, and the standard Go wasip1 runtime imports it. Returning ENOSYS from `poll_oneoff` may abort Go and TinyGo guests: the Go wasip1 runtime is understood to throw when `poll_oneoff` fails in its sleep and idle paths, though this has not been verified against the research. Name `sched_yield` (success). For `poll_oneoff`, choose either a clock-only subscription that returns at once or a trap mapped to RZ-PLG-001, so that the Go/TinyGo scaffold conformance case is deterministic.

'Full reservation makes the Node cap a hard bound on linear memory' holds only for live pages. Unless instances use `WithMemoryCapacityFromMax(true)` (research 2.2), each `memory.grow` reallocates and copies, so the old buffers stay garbage in the Go heap until the next GC. The live linear memory also raises the GC heap goal. State the allocation mode, and describe how the Plugin reservation interacts with GOGC and GOMEMLIMIT in the Data plane memory sum.

The '`state.read` reference pool ramp from 1 to 25 instances | 250 ms or less (target)' row does not match '40 at the maximum' creation throughput (hypothesis): at 40 per second, 24 instances take 600 ms. Either bound `rz_configure` more tightly for pools that need a fast ramp, or state that the ramp target assumes typical creation cost.

Because compiled code is kept in memory only and compiles run one at a time, every restart, scale-out and Zero-Downtime Upgrade recompiles the whole Bundle before `/readyz`. During a handover, both processes also hold their own Plugin reservations and compiled code. Add a boot compile-time row for the reference Bundle (target). Allow more compile workers while the Node is not yet ready. Note in Capacity planning that a handover can double Plugin memory.

With 1,000 serialized contexts on one instance, a call that runs to the 5 ms timeout blocks the other 999 streams, and the resulting discard loses all of their state. State a wait bound on the per-instance mutex (for example 1 ms, then RZ-PLG-005), and name the head-of-line case in OQ-wasm-plugin-system-17.
